title:
This abstract type is the base of all caches that are tag-specific.
It should be used for all server caches that refer to or depend on the state of metadata.

Tag caches function like singletons (their methods are static), but the entries are tag-specific
(get may return different values for actions running against different tags). This means users of the cache
do not need to consider the tag; they always build and access entries for the "current tag".

Note that MetadataCacheOld is parametrized by the type of its entries. These entries are computed based,
at least in part, on metadata (which is why they are tag-specific). The type used for the entry
is specific to each cache, with the fields computed in whatever form is most natural for consumption.

Values that are expensive to compute can also be stored in the database. If the entry type is
naturally persistable as an included type, it will be persisted in the tag. As per usual DB engine rules,
fields marked with `@db(persistable=false)` or defined as `native` will not be persisted.

In addition to caching, implementations will often want to support an incremental validator.
This validator maintains "metadata issues" that will be reported back during provisioning and
are available to development tools.

To implement a cache:
 - extend MetadataCacheOld, binding the parameter appropriately
 - implement the produce function
 - implement a {@link MetadataListener}

@see MetadataListener
